Title: Nanta: Pan Borneo highway contracts cannot be terminated arbitrarily
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Contracts of companies involved in the construction of the Pan Borneo Highway cannot be terminated arbitrarily, as delays in individual work packages are not necessarily caused solely by the contractors' shortcomings.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said that when contractors applied for an extension of time (EOT), the Works Ministry (KKR) had to assess whether the delays were caused by constraints on the part of government agencies or other factors.
He said only one contractor had so far had its contract terminated over delays in the project, following a comprehensive assessment.
"When contractors apply for an extension of time, we have to carefully examine whether the problem is their fault, as some delays may also be caused by factors on our side.
"For example, a contractor may be ready to begin work but cannot access the site because land acquisition and compensation matters have yet to be settled by the relevant government department," he said.
Nanta said this after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV's 'Ruang Bicara' programme that discussed strengthening national infrastructure towards sustainable development here today.
Apart from land compensation issues, Nanta said construction work could also be held up if utility infrastructure, such as water pipes and underground cables, had yet to be relocated by the relevant parties, as proceeding with the work could risk damaging them.
To avoid further delays, he said KKR had proactively set up monitoring committees, a steering committee and task forces to address the issues.
"Through these platforms, problems at construction sites can be raised and solutions decided immediately, without having to wait unnecessarily and waste time due to poor coordination," he said.
Nanta said oversight of the projects was also being strengthened through regular site visits by the ministry's top management, as well as close cooperation with the Sabah and Sarawak Public Works Departments.
To date, only 11.4 per cent of the work packages under the Pan Borneo Highway project in Sabah have been completed, more than 10 years after its implementation began, while the Sarawak stretch is nearing completion. — BERNAMA

Title: Schools evacuated across Italy after bomb threats
Article:
ROME: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger."
Meloni said she had called a government meeting later on Wednesday after 312 schools received threats, according to Italian media.--AFP

Title: RM488mil modular data centre in Senai expected to be completed in Q1 2027
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU: EPG's Malaysian Free Industrial Zone (FIZ) factory EPG Modular Data Center worth RM488 million in Senai Airport City (SAC) is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.
EPG announced in a statement today that the installation of the final structural beams of the factory has been completed, marking the completion of the facility's building structure.
The factory, located in an integrated industrial development area of ​​approximately 1,100 hectares in Iskandar Malaysia, covers an area of ​​107,450 square metres, including 70,000 square metres of production space.
As part of the SAC Phase 3 development, the facility is expected to be one of the largest modular data centre (MDC) manufacturing bases in the sector in terms of production capacity, as well as providing over 800 professional and technical job opportunities when fully operational.
EPG founder and chairman Alick Wan said the FIZ plant is an important step in bringing the company's manufacturing capabilities closer to its customers and the markets it serves.
"By combining advanced manufacturing and close collaboration with local partners, we are developing a responsive operating base in Malaysia, while creating a model that can be adapted to customer needs in other markets," he said.
Meanwhile, Senai Airport City chief executive officer Gan Seng Keong said EPG's investment is a significant addition to the growing data centre manufacturing ecosystem at SAC.
According to EPG, the factory's master plan includes five buildings for sheet metal production, power transfer unit (PTU) products, diesel generators, final assembly as well as research and development (R&D) and offices.
The factory will integrate advanced automation equipment, intelligent control systems and automatic welding technology with the production line expected to achieve at least 80 per cent automation rate.
EPG also intends to gradually develop cooperation with local suppliers and increase the involvement of Malaysian companies in its supply chain.

Title: Selangor plans country's first wakaf hospital
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Perbadanan Wakaf Selangor is planning to develop the country's first wakaf hospital to address a shortage of hospital beds and treatment facilities.
Its chairman, Tan Sri Syed Zainal Abidin Syed Mohamed Tahir, said several possible locations had been identified, including Bangi, Shah Alam and Kota Kemuning.
He said the proposal was still at an early stage, with discussions ongoing with agencies under the Selangor  government.
"It is our aspiration to develop a wakaf hospital. In Selangor, there are not enough beds for patients," he said.
He was speaking after launching the Year End Wakaf 2026 campaign, organised by Perbadanan Wakaf Selangor in collaboration with Bank Islam Malaysia Berhad.
The proposed hospital would serve not only general patients but also benefit asnaf groups in Selangor, he said.
He said serving the asnaf was among the responsibilities entrusted to the corporation.
Perbadanan Wakaf Selangor also plans to develop other wakaf assets, including wakaf elderly care homes, as Selangor moves towards becoming an ageing state.
Separately, Syed Zainal said the corporation was targeting RM100 million in cash wakaf and corporate wakaf collections this year through efforts to raise awareness and encourage greater participation from the public and corporate sector.

Title: Melaka polls: Investments to create jobs for Melaka people, says Ab Rauf
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Investments coming into Melaka are expected to generate employment opportunities for the people, particularly as companies need workers to operate their businesses, said Melaka Barisan Nasional  chairman Datuk Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said the state government had a responsibility to prepare a skilled workforce to meet the needs of investors and ensure that the people benefited from the investments.
"Investments certainly reflect the job opportunities available and the workforce that the state government will provide.
"This will also create employment opportunities for the people," he said after visiting the Ayer Limau state constituency operations room today.
Also present was BN candidate for Ayer Limau, Datuk Hameed Mytheen Kunju Basheer.
Ab Rauf was responding to a statement by Melaka Pakatan Harapan chairman Adly Zahari, who said investments in the state should translate into quality jobs with higher salaries, particularly for young people seeking to build their careers in Melaka.
Adly was reported to have said that the benefits of economic development should be measured by their impact on workers, including income stability and opportunities for career advancement.
In a separate development, Ab Rauf expressed satisfaction with the preparedness of the party machinery in Ayer Limau, with three days remaining before polling day in the Melaka state election on Saturday.
"We are now making a final push towards polling day on Saturday, which the people of Melaka have been looking forward to as they prepare to make their choice.
"I can see that the readiness of the machinery and the people in Ayer Limau to cast their votes is at a very good level," he said.

Title: Ringgit ends mostly higher against major and regional currencies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended mostly higher on Wednesday against major and regional currencies but eased against the greenback amid renewed expectations of a hike in US interest rates.
This comes following stronger-than-expected US inflation data.
At 6pm, the local currency fell to 4.0710/0745 against the greenback from 4.0540/0580 at Tuesday's close.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit fell by almost 0.45 per cent against the greenback today as stronger-than-expected US inflation fuelled expectations of a rate hike in December.
"The odds of a rate hike at the December Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting rose to more than 80 per cent after the October US consumer price index (CPI) reading came in above expectations," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said the prospect of a 50-basis-point increase in the federal funds rate at the December meeting lifted demand for the greenback, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) rising 0.18 per cent to 102.412 points.
The ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened against the euro to 4.5343/5382 from 4.5514/5559 at Tuesday's close and appreciated vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4246/4293 from 5.4425/4479, and was marginally higher against the Japanese yen at 2.5609/5632 from 2.5642/5669.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against its Asean peers.
It appreciated against the Thai baht to 12.0963/1117 from 12.1337/1497, climbed vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 224.3/224.6 from 224.4/224.7 and rose against the Philippine peso to 6.43/6.44 from 6.44/6.45.

Title: Melaka polls: Packed schedule does not stop Rais from visiting flood victims
Article:
MELAKA: Even with his campaign schedule in Sungai Udang running at full pace, Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Rais Yasin took time to visit families affected by floods in Kampung Gapam, Bemban, Jasin, last night.
The floods affected seven houses, prompting Rais, who previously served as the state's senior executive councillor for housing, local government, drainage, climate change and disaster management, to visit the area.
He said the welfare of the people must take priority, even with only two days left before polling day.
He added that his visit was not merely to offer support to the affected families but also to identify the necessary follow-up measures.
"Responsibilities must be fulfilled even when we are busy campaigning. The people's problems must take priority.
"As a representative of the state government, I came to Bemban to meet the affected families. The least we can do is be there for those affected," he said when met after engaging with the Chinese community in Sungai Udang here today.
Rais said the recurring floods in the area warranted further investigation, particularly into possible links with development activities in the surrounding area.
He said the state government had directed the local authorities to take action against two developers undertaking projects there, including ordering them to suspend work until measures were taken to address residents' concerns.
"There are guidelines which stipulate that developers cannot carry out development without obtaining approval from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), the Land Office and all relevant technical agencies," he said.
Rais said the flooding issue should not be taken lightly, noting that Melaka still had 102 flood hotspots, compared with more than 150 previously.
He said efforts to reduce the number of flood-prone areas would continue to ensure residents' safety, particularly during periods of heavy rain.

Title: MMAG Holdings' bank accounts freed from AMLA restrictions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MMAG Holdings Bhd said restrictions imposed on certain bank accounts belonging to the company and its subsidiaries under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) have been lifted.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said the affected accounts are no longer subject to restrictions previously imposed by the Royal Malaysia Police's (PDRM) Anti-Money Laundering Investigation Team.
The development follows the group's earlier announcements on March 10 and March 17, 2026, concerning the freezing of the accounts.
MMAG shares closed one sen, or 33.33 per cent, higher at four sen today.

Title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal crash on Jalan Kuching
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A car washer was brought before the Magistrate's Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month.
Mohamad Imran Taj Maloor, 32, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan.
No plea was recorded from the accused, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44 am on Nov 4.
The charge is framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of up to 40 years and, where the death penalty is not imposed, not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Vivi Asnita Zaina'Larifin, while the accused was represented by lawyer Azleen Farahannis.
No bail was allowed, and the court set Jan 28 next year for mention.
Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.
"As a result of the collision, the lorry veered onto the left road shoulder while its driver, a 39-year-old Indonesian man, suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene," he said.
According to Mohd Zamzuri, an EBA II breath test recorded a blood alcohol reading of 61 mg/100ml for the car driver, while his passenger recorded 67 mg/100ml. — BERNAMA

Title: JAC rolls out first locally assembled PHEV pickup
Article:
EVOLVELECTRIC Motors Sdn Bhd has launched the JAC T9 plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) petrol, introducing what it says is Malaysia's first locally assembled plug-in hybrid pickup truck.
The JAC T9 PHEV Petrol is currently the only plug-in hybrid pickup available in the Malaysian market, combining a conventional 4x4 setup with electric propulsion and extended driving range.
It is offered in two variants, with the Adventure version priced at RM162,888 and the standard customer-oriented variant at RM154,888, excluding road tax and insurance.
The Adventure variant comes with all-terrain tyres and black alloy rims.
Power comes from a 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine paired with an electric four-wheel-drive dual-motor system and a 4DHT hybrid transmission.
The combined powertrain produces 360kW and 1,000Nm of torque.
The front electric motor generates 130kW and 300Nm, while the rear motor delivers 150kW and 340Nm.
A 31.2kWh lithium iron phosphate battery supplied by Gotion High-Tech provides an all-electric range of up to 100km under the New European Driving Cycle.
The pickup has a claimed fuel consumption of 1.6 litres per 100km under the applicable test conditions.
The T9 PHEV also retains conventional pickup capabilities, with a braked towing capacity of up to 3,500kg and a wading depth of 550mm.
Its Advanced Driver-Assistance System 2.0 includes adaptive cruise control, traffic jam assist, automatic emergency braking, blind spot detection, speed limit assistance and a driver monitoring system.
Other features include a 360-degree around-view monitor and transparent chassis view.
The model has received a five-star rating from the Australasian New Car Assessment Program.
Evolvelectric Motors chief executive officer Lau Yit Mun said the model is aimed at customers seeking a vehicle that can serve both business and family requirements.
"The JAC T9 PHEV is more than just a pickup truck.
"Its Vehicle-to-Load function offers a discharge capacity of up to 15kW, enabling it to double as a mobile power station," he said.
The vehicle offers Eco, Standard and Sport drive modes, alongside Snow, Sand, Mud, Rock and off-road cruise terrain settings.
It supports both DC fast and AC charging.
DC charging from 15 per cent to 80 per cent takes about 30 minutes, while AC charging over the same range takes between 3.5 and 5.5 hours.
The T9 PHEV is available in five colours and comes with an eight-year or 150,000km battery warranty, alongside a seven-year or 150,000km vehicle warranty.

Title: Betamek's Q2 net profits fell 32pct; declares 1.25 sen dividend per share
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:Betamek Bhd's net profit fell 32.1 per cent in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, at RM7.1 million, from RM10.4 million a year ago, due to higher operating expenses and lower margins.
Despite the decline in profits, the group declared a second interim single-tier dividend of 1.25 sen per share, payable on Dec 7.
The dividend will be paid to shareholders whose names appear in the record of depositors on Nov 26.
This brings its cumulative dividend for the financial year ending 2027 to 2.50 sen per share, following the first interim dividend of 1.25 sen paid in August.
Revenue for the quarter increased by RM9.02 million or 12.44 per cent to RM81.49 million, mainly due to higher export sales, which increased by RM9.99 million, partially offset by slightly lower local sales, Betamek said.
Its profit before tax (PBT) declined 25.7 per cent to RM9.3 million during the quarter, as gross profit (GP) margin decreased to 16.7 per cent, compared with 22.74 per cent in the preceding year's corresponding quarter.
"The lower GP margin was mainly attributable to a change in product mix, with a higher contribution from lower-margin export sales and a lower contribution from connectivity modules, which carry higher margins than the group's traditional automotive products.
"The balance of the decrease in PBT was mainly due to higher other operating expenses, including net foreign exchange losses," said Betamek.
For the first half to Sept 30, 2026, the group's net profit fell three per cent to RM15.30 million from RM15.78 million a year earlier, despite stronger revenue contributions from export and local sales.
The original design manufacturer and electronics manufacturing services provider's revenue increased 24.7 per cent to RM161.31 million from RM129.35 million in the corresponding period last year.
The growth was mainly driven by higher export sales, which increased by RM22.46 million, while local sales rose by RM9.49 million.
Vehicle audio and video products remained the group's largest revenue contributor at RM94.94 million, followed by vehicle accessories at RM51.37 million.
Connectivity modules contributed RM7.12 million, while non-automotive products accounted for RM7.88 million.
Betamek executive director Muhammad Fauzi Abd Ghani said the first-half performance reflected the underlying strength of its business and its continued relevance in the evolving automotive landscape.
"We are focused on building a more competitive and resilient group by enhancing our technological capabilities and maintaining high manufacturing standards.
"We are also positioning Betamek to capture opportunities arising from increasingly sophisticated vehicle technologies.
"These priorities will support our ability to meet customers' evolving requirements and create sustainable value over the long term," he said in a statement.
Export sales accounted for approximately 19.3 per cent of the group's total revenue during the period.
Revenue from Hong Kong increased to RM29.03 million from RM6.55 million a year earlier, while revenue from Malaysia rose to RM130.12 million from RM120.62 million.
Looking ahead, Betamek remains optimistic about its prospects, supported by continued automotive demand and increasing electronics content in vehicles.
It also sees opportunities arising from the government's focus on greater local content.
The group secured a three-year renewal of its Supplier Competitiveness Level 5 certification from the Malaysia Automotive, Robotics and IoT Institute, extending its validity until 2029.
It said it would remain mindful of foreign exchange volatility, raw material costs and product mix.
The group will maintain its focus on cost discipline, operational efficiency and diversification.

Title: Oppstar recorded narrower net loss in Q2 as revenue surges 71pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Oppstar Bhd registered narrower net loss of RM62,000 in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27), compared with RM3.2 million a year ago, as revenue surged 71 per cent to RM12.6 million.
The higher revenue translated into RM7,000 profit before tax during the quarter, a sharp turn from a loss before tax of RM3.32 million in the same quarter last year, the integrated circuit (IC) design company said.
The robust year-on-year performance was predominantly fueled by the IC design segment.
Revenue from specific design services grew by RM3.79 million due to heightened demand for engineering services, while post-silicon validation services saw a RM1.45 million increase driven by customer demand, said Oppstar.
Despite the top-line growth, Oppstar faced higher operational expenses. Cost of sales increased by RM1.03 million, primarily due to higher labour costs, though this was partially offset by lower travelling and design tool subscription costs.
Administrative expenses also rose by RM0.37 million due to increased personnel and travelling costs. However, the bottom line was supported by a RM0.58 million reversal of impairment loss on trade receivables following a successful collection from a customer.
While year-on-year figures reflect strong growth, Oppstar experienced a 20.64 per cent sequential decline in revenue, dropping from RM15.86 million in the immediate preceding quarter to RM12.59 million.
This contraction was mainly attributed to a RM4 million decrease in revenue from turnkey design services due to the timing of project recognition. Consequently, the profit before tax also moderated from RM4.41 million in the preceding quarter to RM7,000.
Looking ahead, Oppstar expects the current financial year to outperform the preceding year, underpinned by strong, AI-driven demand in the semiconductor industry. The structural shift toward AI-related chips is widening the company's project pipeline.
To capitalize on this trend, Oppstar intends to move up the value chain, transitioning from a predominantly service-based model to a more integrated role within the AI ecosystem.
This includes targeting high-value turnkey design projects and exploring selective collaborations in AI hardware development, specifically for architectures like AI accelerators and Neural Processing Units (NPUs).
However, the company noted that the global shortage of skilled semiconductor engineers remains a structural challenge, placing upward pressure on remuneration and overall personnel costs.

Title: Foreign driver arrested after driving against traffic in Kempas
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A foreign driver was arrested after driving against traffic and sideswiping a Honda Civic in Kempas.
The accident led to an exchange between the drivers, which was captured in a video posted online.
The 32-year-old was driving a Toyota Harrier along Jalan Banjaran Utama yesterday when he entered the opposing lane and collided with a Honda Civic driven by a 26-year-old Malaysian.
Johor Baru (North) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrol Anuar Nor said the impact caused the Harrier to veer off to the left side of the road.
Police will seek a remand order for the foreigner to facilitate investigations under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving.
The offence carries a jail term of up to five years, a fine of between RM5,000 and RM15,000, and disqualification from holding or obtaining a driving licence for at least five years upon conviction.
In the footage, the Honda driver is seen repeatedly demanding an explanation from the foreign driver over the collision.

Title: Pejuang proposes phased closure of UNHCR office in Malaysia
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang) has submitted memorandums to the Home and Foreign Ministries calling for a comprehensive review of refugee management in Malaysia, including the possibility of gradually closing the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in the country.
Two representatives from Pejuang Wilayah Persekutuan, Ena Awil and Nana Nordin, were present at both ministries to hand over the memorandums.
The memorandums were addressed to Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
When contacted, Pejuang information chief Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali called on the government to consider gradually transferring refugee registration, identification, monitoring and case management responsibilities to Malaysian authorities.
He stressed that any decision to close UNHCR operations should only be implemented after a comprehensive assessment and the establishment of an effective government-managed system.
"Based on the memorandum, the proposal is aimed at ensuring that policies governing refugees and asylum seekers are determined according to Malaysian laws, national interests, public safety and administrative capabilities.
"The government should first evaluate the legal, diplomatic, financial, security and administrative implications of closing UNHCR operations," he said.
He also called for an official transition plan identifying the lead agencies, division of responsibilities, manpower requirements, estimated costs and implementation timeline.
The memorandum outlined 10 key demands, including an independent audit of existing refugee management mechanisms and the establishment of a comprehensive government-controlled refugee database.
The proposed audit would examine identity verification, registration procedures, complaints and appeals mechanisms, data security, funding, public service costs and refugee resettlement outcomes.
Rafique said the party also proposed closer coordination between the Home Ministry, Immigration Department, police, National Registration Department, welfare agencies and state authorities.
"Any transfer of responsibilities must not result in gaps in monitoring, missing records, overlapping responsibilities or uncontrolled delays in handling refugee cases.
"Among other proposals was a feasibility study on controlled temporary accommodation facilities for refugees, subject to legal, security, financial and welfare considerations," he said.
He also urged the government to clarify employment regulations for UNHCR document holders, including whether they could legally work in Malaysia and the conditions governing such employment.
The memorandum called for greater transparency in healthcare expenditure involving refugees, including a breakdown of government spending, user payments, subsidies and donor contributions.
"The party is also seeking stronger enforcement against suspected illegal business activities, document forgery, misuse of identities and unlawful employment.
"Enforcement action, however, must be based on evidence and applicable laws rather than assumptions about particular communities," he said.
He added that the party had called for the regular publication of accurate crime statistics, warning that isolated offences should not be used to generalise about the entire refugee population.
On international obligations, the memorandum acknowledged that Malaysia was not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol.
"The government must continue to consider applicable domestic laws and other international legal obligations, including relevant protections against returning individuals to places where they could face persecution or serious harm."

Title: IGP: 35 Police personnel recognised for rejecting and reporting corruption this year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 35 police officers and personnel have been recognised this year for their firmness and courage in rejecting and reporting acts of corruption, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.
He said that of the total, six received the Inspector-General of Police's Letter of Appreciation, 13 received Certificates of Appreciation and Financial Rewards from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and 16 received MACC Certificates of Appreciation.
He said that based on MACC statistics, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) was among the government agencies with the highest number of recipients of such recognition, involving 437 officers and personnel between 2012 and 2025.
"This achievement demonstrates the firm stand taken by members of the force in combating corruption, a stance that should be emulated by all police personnel," he said at the launch of the 2026 PDRM Integrity Month celebration here today.
Khalid stressed that integrity must begin with oneself by upholding the values of honesty, responsibility and diligence in every decision made.
He said that as the country's law enforcement agency, every action taken by members of the force reflected police credibility, professionalism and authority in the eyes of the public.
As such, he called for the continuous strengthening of good values through more intensive education and training to mould police personnel who consistently uphold the trust placed in them and understand the limits of their authority. — BERNAMA

Title: War cost Gulf over US$200bil in damage, US$790bil losses until 2030
Article:
DUBAI: The US-Iran war will cost Gulf countries more than US$200 billion in damage and economic losses could reach nearly four times that amount by 2030, insurer Allianz Trade said on Wednesday.
Gulf countries bore the brunt of Teheran's wrath after the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb 28, triggering the war.
In retaliation, Iran restricted shipping in the key strait of Hormuz and struck civilian infrastructure including airports, seaports, energy facilities, landmarks and American assets in the US-allied countries.
"Physical damage across the region is assessed just above US$200bn, mostly concentrated in Hormuz-locked economies, especially in energy infrastructure," the insurer said in a report.
More than 80 energy facilities were hit in the war, mostly in Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain, the report said, with a third of them "severely damaged."
Beyond physical damage to energy infrastructure, the war has affected other sectors like tourism and real estate, which will see slower growth over the years.
"The total cost of the war for the GCC is set to reach US$790bn, a cumulative gap of 5.9 per cent of GDP relative to the pre-war trend through 2030," the report said.
"This reflects the cumulative loss of economic output over 2026-30, the difference between what the region was forecast to produce on its pre war-growth trend and what it is now projected to produce post-war," it said.
To make up for the losses, Gulf states are expected to reallocate sovereign wealth fund capital to domestic projects.
External surplus is expected to be halved but will be "partially offset with increased repatriation of sovereign wealth fund capital... of around US$120bn of extra domestic investment through 2030 to the detriment of international investment," the report said.
"The war accelerates the need to spend more domestically as government priorities have shifted away from mega-projects towards resilience - and security-related ones," it added.
Gulf states are expected to raise their domestic infrastructure and defence spending to US$380-US$400bn through 2030, the report said, providing "an opportunity of around US$160bn for private and foreign investors."
Despite war and restricted access to Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab strait, Saudi oil giant Aramco announced a 34.6 per cent surge in third-quarter net profit last week, as Iran's restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz drives oil prices up.
The IMF expects Saudi Arabia, one of the world's biggest oil producers, to end the year with a 3.3 per cent contraction in GDP, five percentage points lower than its previous forecast in July.

Title: Zahid tells Mat Sabu to surrender ministerial allowances too [WATCH]
Article:
AYER KEROH: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has backed Mohamad Sabu's decision to forfeit his entire ministerial salary to support groups campaigning for equal house arrest rights for prisoners.
Zahid said the Amanah president should also give up his ministerial allowances if he genuinely wanted to support the cause.
"That is good, it is a fine proposal," Zahid told reporters at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC).
"However, if the intention is genuinely to assist, I hope he surrenders not just his salary, but his allowances as well.
"A minister's basic salary is modest, but the allowances are substantial — he shouldn't keep the allowances," he added.
Earlier today, Mohamad, popularly known as Mat Sabu, announced in Jasin that he would forfeit his entire monthly ministerial salary of RM11,900 until the dissolution of Parliament.
He said the
money would go
towards funding civil society groups and legal practitioners advocating equal treatment under the law.
Mohamad called for a formal legal mechanism allowing all convicts to serve half their sentences in prison and the remaining half under house arrest, arguing that such arrangements should not be an exclusive privilege for high-profile political figures or VVIPs.
He also said he had no personal grudge against former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak or his family. His decision came amid public debate over executive provisions and house arrest procedures.

Title: Sri Lanka launches pilot of Chinese flying taxi service
Article:
COLOMBO: Sri Lanka has authorised a Chinese manufacturer to begin testing a pilotless two-seater air taxi, authorities announced Wednesday at a flight demonstration in Colombo.
The Civil Aviation Authority said a licence had been granted to EHang to test its two-seater, pilotless electric aircraft with vertical take-off and landing capability.
The company demonstrated its EH216-S aircraft with a short flight, carrying Ports and Aviation Minister Anura Karunathilaka and his deputy Janitha Ruwan Kodithuwakku as the first passengers.
Kodithuwakku said Sri Lanka was also joining a race among more than a dozen countries to introduce passenger-drone services.
[[nid:1575541]]
"Many countries around the world are trying to achieve this goal... Sri Lanka is now part of that race as well," Kodithuwakku told reporters after his brief flight.
He said testing could continue for about five months before commercial services may be permitted.
Promoters hope to launch an air-taxi service between the airport and the Colombo city centre, a journey that takes about half an hour by car.
Sri Lankan officials said the EHang EH216-S is powered by 16 electric motors and 16 propellers.
It carries 12 battery packs, has a maximum take-off weight of 620 kilogrammes and can operate for about 25 minutes, covering a distance of up to 30 kilometres.

Title: United Plantations reports 43pct higher net profits in Q3; warns of workers shortages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: United Plantations Bhd's net profit rose 43.1 per cent to RM290.93 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 from RM203.28 million a year ago, on the back of higher production volume.
Revenue for the quarter under review climbed 6.7 per cent year-on-year to RM722.22 million from RM677.08 million last year, while profit before tax jumped 34.8 per cent to RM380.9 million.
For the nine-month period, the company's earnings increased 4.8 per cent to RM645.58 million from RM615.92 million a year ago, on the back of 9.4 per cent higher revenue at RM2 billion.
According to United Plantations, both the plantation and refinery segments benefitted from higher production volumes of crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel, as well as firm selling prices.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company noted revenue for its plantation segment rose 6.1 per cent to RM1.25 billion in the cumulative nine-month period due to higher production volumes of CPO and palm kernel which increased 5.7 per cent and 10.8 per cent respectively.
The average selling price of palm kernel during the period rose 4.9 per cent to RM3,405 per tonne while CPO saw a marginal decline to RM4,251 per tonne.
Revenue from the refinery segment increased  12.1 per cent to RM1.3 billion driven by higher average selling prices.
Despite the higher revenue, the segment recorded a lower pre-tax profit of RM35.9 million, mainly attributable to timing differences between raw material hedging transactions and the delivery of finished goods.
Looking ahead, the company said one of the key factors influencing palm oil prices will be the development of Malaysian palm oil inventories, which could approach historically high levels of around four million tonnes towards year-end.
"Under normal circumstances, such elevated stocks would exert considerable downward pressure on prices.
"However, the market appears increasingly focused on the potential tightening of supply during 2027 again, a function of higher Biodiesel production and a lower production in Indonesia arising from the monster El Nino this July to October," it said.
United Plantations added that while the current labour situation remains manageable during the seasonally lower production months, the continued freeze on the recruitment of guest workers will present serious challenges as the industry approaches its next production peak in March/April 2027.
"The group remains hopeful that the government will consider the industry's labour requirements to help minimise field losses, safeguard production and export earnings," it said.
The company declared a single-tier interim dividend of 30 sen per share and a special dividend of 15 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 with both dividends payable on Dec 8.

Title: 4 injured as factory van hits broken-down bus on Johor highway
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Four workers heading to Singapore were injured when their factory van crashed into a broken-down workers' bus on the Eastern Dispersal Link (EDL).
The collision occurred at 4.45am at Km0.2 of the highway, involving a van driven by a 28-year-old Malaysian man carrying three passengers.
Johor Baru (South) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hishan Mohd Shaffei said investigations found that the van was travelling towards Singapore when it approached the stationary factory bus, which had broken down in the right lane.
The driver is believed to have failed to notice the bus in time and could not avoid the collision on the slightly curved stretch of road.
The van hit the bus's rear left side.
The van driver sustained injuries to his body and legs.
The three passengers also suffered injuries, including head wounds.
Azrul Hishan said the case was being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for careless driving.

Title: Southern Score Builders' subsidiary secured data centre electrical works in Port Dickson
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Southern Score Builders Bhd, through its 51 per cent-owned subsidiary SJEE Engineering Sdn Bhd, has secured two subcontract agreements worth a combined RM146.8 million for electrical works at two data centre projects in Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan.
The contracts involve the construction, completion, testing and commissioning of Electrical Package 3 and other associated works for the two projects.
The first project carries a subcontract sum of RM67.41 million, while the second is valued at RM79.39 million.
Southern Score said the first project's Phase 1 substantial completion is scheduled for Oct 22, 2027, followed by Phase 2 on Jan 21, 2028.
For the second project, Phase 1 substantial completion is targeted for Jan 10, 2028, while Phase 2 is scheduled for April 10, 2028.
"The projects are expected to contribute positively to the net assets and earnings per share of the company and its group of companies for the financial year ending June 30,
2027 onwards until the completion of the projects," it said.

Title: Monash University showcases postgraduate pathways for Malaysians at Peak TRX
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:
Students and working professionals looking to advance their careers through postgraduate education can explore their options at Postgraduate Education Advancement & Knowledge (Peak) TRX, organised by Monash University on Nov 21, 2026.
The event will be held at Kimpton Naluria, Kuala Lumpur, and aims to help prospective postgraduate students understand the study pathways available and how further education can support their personal and professional aspirations.
EXPLORING NEW PATHWAYS
As industries evolve and workplace demands change, postgraduate education offers opportunities to deepen expertise, broaden knowledge and develop skills aligned with career goals.
However, choosing the right programme requires careful consideration of professional aspirations, areas of interest and long-term career plans.
PERSONALISED GUIDANCE
A key feature of the event is the opportunity for attendees to engage directly with academic experts and receive guidance on suitable postgraduate study options.
These interactions will allow prospective students to learn more about their areas of interest, clarify questions about further education and consider how different programmes align with their professional objectives.
The event is open to a broad audience, including fresh graduates considering their next academic step, working professionals looking to strengthen their expertise and people exploring new career directions.
SUPPORTING CAREER GROWTH
For those already in the workforce, postgraduate studies can build on existing experience while developing the knowledge and capabilities needed to navigate an increasingly dynamic employment landscape.
Beyond academic qualifications, continued learning can also help people strengthen their adaptability, explore new areas of specialisation and prepare for emerging opportunities in their respective fields.
Through Peak TRX, Monash University Malaysia aims to provide prospective students with information and guidance to help them make informed decisions about their education and career pathways.
For further information and registration details, visit the university's official
website
.

Title: Zahid eyes BN-PN sweep in Melaka, calls for 'blue wave' [WATCH]
Article:
AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has expressed confidence that the BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN) alliance can secure all 28 Melaka state seats, urging voters to turn their support into a "blue wave" when polls open this Saturday.
Speaking at the Kemas Pre-Tahfiz Grand Khatam and Digital Engagement ceremony at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Zahid seized on the light-blue stage backdrop to deliver an impromptu rallying call.
Addressing thousands of educators, community members and parents, Zahid said: "Look in front of us, at this board, at this slide — the blue is as brilliant and bright as the open sky. God willing, we will continue to turn the state of Melaka completely blue this coming Saturday."
"I am not campaigning here, but this blue colour will illuminate all 28 Melaka state seats," he added, before leading the crowd in chants of "Kita Geng Biru".
A total of 79 candidates are contesting all 28 seats in the 16th Melaka election, comprising 11 straight fights, 11 three-cornered contests and six four-cornered battles.
Under an electoral pact, BN is contesting 23 seats, while its ally PN is fielding candidates in the remaining five, allowing the two coalitions to contest all 28 seats collectively.
They face competition from Pakatan Harapan (PH), which is contesting 24 seats, as well as Bersama (16), Bersatu (7), Putra (1) and independent candidates.
Speaking at a press conference on the sidelines of the event, Zahid said the official campaign period was entering its final stretch, with less than 72 hours remaining before it ended at midnight on Nov 13.
"We have just half a day today, tomorrow, and the day after — under 72 hours until campaigning officially concludes at midnight on the 13th," he said.
He thanked all contesting political parties for adhering to campaign ethics, saying the run-up to polling day had been exceptionally peaceful.
"I am grateful that all contesting parties have respected campaign ethics and maintained good decorum," he said.
"Although the atmosphere has been very calm compared to previous state or by-elections, we hope that on voting day itself, no untoward incidents will occur. We have full confidence in the capabilities of our security forces and the diligence shown by the Election Commission."
Zahid said BN and PN had presented an election manifesto featuring 113 pledges for Melaka voters, anchored on key pillars addressing the needs of all age groups, ethnicities, faiths, cultures and languages.
"Melaka has been governed well, and we hope voters will place their trust and support in the BN candidates we have fielded," he said.

Title: Anwar, Koh pay tribute to Chet Singh, Penang industrialisation pioneer
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang's emergence as a world-class electrical and electronics hub was shaped in large part by former Penang Development Corporation (PDC) general manager Datuk Seri Chet Singh Karam Singh, who died yesterday aged 90.
In a condolence message on Facebook, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim paid tribute to Chet Singh, describing him as a key figure in the state's industrial development.
"As the first general manager of PDC, the late Chet Singh played an important role in spearheading the development of industrial areas, attracting international investments and transforming Penang into a world-class electrical and electronics hub," he said.
Anwar said Chet Singh's contributions had also created employment opportunities, stimulated economic growth and laid important foundations for the country's industrial development.
"The late Chet Singh's contributions and legacy in advancing Malaysia's industrial and economic development will continue to be remembered," he added.
Former Penang chief minister Tan Sri Dr Koh Tsu Koon described Chet Singh as the engineer of Penang's industrialisation.
In extending his condolences to Chet Singh's widow, Datin Seri Bharjan Kaur, and the family, Koh said Penang had lost a great man.
"As Penang's second chief minister, Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu, has rightly been known as the architect of Penang's industrialisation, Chet was undoubtedly the engineer who put the stones and mortar in place for its realisation," he said.
Koh first met Chet Singh after being elected Tanjung member of Parliament in the 1982 general election, when he sought his assistance for residents and social and religious organisations affected by the Komtar development project.
"Despite his rather stern look, he actually had a heart of gold and was very sympathetic and helpful, especially to the poor and disadvantaged," Koh recalled.
He said their working relationship deepened after he was appointed political secretary to Lim following the 1986 general election.
When Koh became chief minister following the 1990 general election, Chet Singh provided crucial guidance.
"He accompanied me on my first investment mission to Silicon Valley in California, introducing me to our key investors and guiding me on how to impress them to invest or expand," Koh said.
After stepping down from PDC in 1992, Chet Singh was succeeded by his deputy, Datuk Mokhtar Haniff, but remained active as an industrial development consultant to less-developed countries.
On Koh's recommendation, Gerakan nominated Chet Singh as a senator in 1995. He served two terms and contributed to parliamentary debates based on his extensive administrative experience.
Chet Singh was also a founding member of the Wawasan Education Foundation, which established Wawasan Open University. He served on its board until stepping down due to illness in 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nvidia's clubby board faces a sticky 'honey pot' test
Article:
REVELATIONS that Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker's board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for the company and concerns about the board's ability to investigate its CEO independently.
Among corporate leaders, "There have definitely been affair scandals and sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No," said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.
Lipton was using a term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest.
Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang's relationship, a day after Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports," according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.
The stakes are high. While it is not clear if Huang violated the company's code of conduct or what penalties Huang could face, its bylaws allow his removal "with or without cause" by the vote of a majority of directors.
The company's advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI superiority. China's Foreign Ministry called the spying claim "a groundless accusation, slander and a smear."
Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as close ties to Trump.
Huang owns 3.6 per cent of Nvidia's stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.
Shares in Nvidia were down six per cent on Tuesday, extending their losses from Monday over fallout from Huang's affair.
Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors.
While the company considers all but Huang independent, three independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark Stevens, for most of that time.
Only two have joined the board since 2021.
The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple's Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.
But the US probe has heightened scrutiny of whether directors who have worked alongside Huang for decades are sufficiently independent to investigate his conduct.
"If you have a figure like Steve Jobs, I think people on Wall Street as well as in Silicon Valley would say they're entitled to some leeway or deference," said Marc Goldstein, head of US research for proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services.
Such deference could now raise questions about whether the board provided sufficient oversight of a CEO whose own judgment has come under scrutiny.
Nvidia said on Sunday that while its board has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry would examine ​all available information.
[[nid:1575516]]
The board said it has confidence in the CEO and his leadership team.
Goldstein said board members running that investigation should be given the latitude to hire their own legal advisers to bolster their credibility.
The company also might consider keeping long-serving directors away from the probe, Goldstein added, to avoid legal challenges from shareholders claiming it wasn't sufficiently independent.
A factor for the board to consider will be whether Huang reported the affair to the company.
Nvidia's code of conduct lists "personal relationships" among the types of activities that may create conflicts of interest for employees, along with activities like taking on outside consulting work, board seats or advisory roles.
"If involved in a situation that could present a perceived or actual conflict of interest, contact Employment Legal for guidance," the document states.
Gil Soffer, a former US Justice Department official and now chair of law firm Katten, said via email a complete and accurate disclosure by Huang would be favourable for his situation now since it "would mean he didn't conceal the relationship, and that the board presumably had the opportunity to evaluate the relationship, set up guardrails and otherwise manage the potential conflict."
Soffer said more public facts are needed to know whether a conflict was in fact created by the relationship, whether the board acted appropriately so far, or what if any punishment of Huang might be justified.
In a bad scenario such as Huang concealing the relationship and engaging in misconduct, "removal could be appropriate," Soffer said.
Huang was paid US$120 million over the past three years, the company's latest proxy shows, largely through stock awards.
The document states, "Our executive officers are 'at-will' employees and we do not have employment, severance or change-in-control agreements with our executive officers."
Yale University management professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld said the company faces additional national-security questions because of the ties between Huang and Trump.
Trump, who has praised Huang, said on Monday that he had spoken to the CEO and thought he would "be in good shape."
The United States has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since ​2022.
Last year the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to resume certain China shipments under arrangements in which the US government receives a cut of the company's China chip sales.
The deal makes any suggestion of foreign espionage more sensitive for both executives and US government officials, Sonnenfeld said.
"That's why you don't want state capitalism arrangements. You don't want the US government to be so involved in private companies," Sonnenfeld said.
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alphabet eyes US$3bil Hong Kong, Singapore bond sale, sources say
Article:
SYDNEY/HONG KONG: Alphabet is looking to raise about US$3 billion equivalent through its first bond sales in Hong Kong and Singapore dollars, two people with knowledge of the matter said, testing Asian investor demand after an AI-led selloff in global markets earlier this month.
One of the people added that the sales would likely raise at least US$2.2 billion, with Alphabet considering minimum sizes of HK$8 billion (US$1 billion) for the Hong Kong dollar portion and S$1.5 billion (US$1.2 billion) for the Singapore dollar portion.
The final size, timing and pricing have not been set, the person added. The people declined to be named as the matter is private.
Alphabet has mandated HSBC and JPMorgan as joint global coordinators, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters earlier Wednesday.
Bank of China (Hong Kong), ICBC (Asia) and Standard Chartered are also working on the Hong Kong dollar sale, while DBS Bank Ltd, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Ltd and United Overseas Bank Ltd are working on the Singapore dollar portion, the sheet showed.
The Hong Kong dollar bonds could have two-, five- and 10-year maturities, while the Singapore dollar bonds could have two-, five-, 10- and 30-year maturities, the sheet showed.
Alphabet did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The sale would add to Alphabet's borrowing this year as it increases spending on data centres and other AI computing infrastructure.
Alphabet said in an Oct 29 filing that it had issued US$45 billion of US dollar-denominated notes and US$35.8 billion of foreign currency notes in the nine months to end-September for general corporate purposes.
Alphabet last week raised EUR6 billion (US$6.7 billion) through a euro-denominated bond sale. It also sold US$25 billion of US dollar bonds in August and A$5.5 billion (US$3.8 billion) Australian dollar bonds in the same month.
Other large technology companies have also tapped debt markets. Last week, Meta completed a US$15 billion US bond sale and Oracle sold US$10 billion of bonds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia lowers December crude palm oil reference price, maintains duty at 10pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has lowered its December crude palm oil reference price, a change that maintains the export duty at 10 per cent, a circular on the Malaysian Palm Oil Board website showed on Wednesday.
The world's second-largest palm oil exporter calculated a reference price of RM4,259.70 (US$1,046.10) per tonne for December. The November reference price was RM4,323.78 a tonne, and incurred a duty of 10 per cent.
The export tax structure starts at 3.0 per cent for crude palm oil in a RM2,250 to RM2,400 per-tonne range. The maximum tax rate is set at 10 per cent when prices exceed RM4,050 ringgit a tonne.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ECRL set to drive Terengganu's economic growth, boost tourism
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), which is scheduled to commence operations in mid-December, is expected to serve as a catalyst for economic growth in Terengganu, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.
He said the state government is encouraging entrepreneurs and business owners to seize the opportunities offered by the new rail network and maximise its potential.
"I believe it can contribute to the economic well-being of the people. Entrepreneurs should explore how they can maximise the benefits of the ECRL, particularly in terms of goods transportation and expanding business activities across different locations," he told reporters after chairing a State Executive Council meeting here today.
Ahmad Samsuri said the state government is also confident that the new rail service will give a further boost to Terengganu's tourism sector by offering visitors a more convenient and flexible travel option.
He said the service would also support the Visit Terengganu Year 2027 (TMT 2027) initiative, which aims to attract more than 15 million tourists to the state.
He added that the state government had held discussions with Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) to ensure that facilities and supporting services around ECRL stations are adequately developed to cater to the expected influx of tourists and visitors from outside the state.
"We have also discussed with MRL the development of areas surrounding the stations, including transit-oriented development (TOD), to ensure that these facilities deliver tangible benefits to tourists, local residents and the business community," he said.
The ECRL is expected to significantly reduce travel time between the East Coast and the Klang Valley, with journeys from Gombak to Kuala Terengganu taking approximately three hours, while the trip from Gombak to Kota Bharu is expected to take about four hours.
The 242-kilometre ECRL alignment in Terengganu features six stations: Chukai, Kemasik, Dungun, Kuala Terengganu, Bandar Permaisuri and Jertih.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nanta confirms he will remain Kapit MP, not contest Sarawak polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Kapit Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi has confirmed that he will continue serving at parliamentary level and will not contest a State Legislative Assembly (DUN) seat in next month’s Sarawak election.
The Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secretary-general said speculation about him contesting at state level arose after a proposal to create a new constituency, DUN Melekun, under the Kapit parliamentary constituency.
However, the works minister said the new constituency could not be used in this election because the boundary changes had not been gazetted.
“Although the Sarawak DUN has approved the addition of seats, the matter has yet to be brought to the Dewan Rakyat for approval.
“So it will not be used in this election, which means I have no state seat to contest,” he told reporters after attending a recording of a Bernama TV programme at Wisma Bernama here today.
On July 7, 2025, the Sarawak DUN passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Membership) Bill 2025, approving 17 additional seats and bringing the total number of state seats to 99.
The number of Sarawak state seats has increased over the years, from 48 in 1969 to 56 in 1985, 62 in 1995, 71 in 2005 and 82 in 2014.
Nanta, who has served six terms as Kapit MP, said not having the opportunity to contest at state level was not an issue, as his priority was to continue serving the people through his existing parliamentary mandate.
He had previously said he did not intend to defend the Kapit parliamentary seat in the next general election to make way for a leadership transition, while also leaving open the possibility of serving at state level if DUN Melekun were created.
Asked about reports that GPS would field 10 per cent new faces in the election, Nanta declined to comment further, saying the decision rested with the party’s top leadership.
The Election Commission has set December 12 as polling day for the Sarawak election, with nominations on November 28 and early voting on December 8. — Bernama

Title: IGP says Prisons Dept responsible for Najib’s home security
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Prisons Department is fully responsible for the security arrangements for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, who has been serving the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here since yesterday.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as a law enforcement agency, maintained close cooperation with the Prisons Department to ensure compliance with the security requirements.
“Since the house (Najib’s residence) falls under the jurisdiction of the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD), I have instructed the IPD to conduct inspections and provide security monitoring from time to time,” he told reporters.
He was speaking after officiating at the 2026 PDRM Integrity Month celebration here today.
Mohd Khalid said PDRM had assigned several officers to assist the Prisons Department throughout the former prime minister’s period of serving the remainder of his sentence at home.
Yesterday, Najib began serving the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest after the High Court here ruled that the order should take effect immediately.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the decision after setting aside an order issued by the High Court Criminal Registry on November 6 against Najib, 73. — AFP

Title: Government steps in with RM15m monthly subsidy as palm oil costs rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government has approved a special incentive of about RM15 million a month under the Cooking Oil Price Control Mechanism (MKHMM) to maintain ceiling prices and ensure a stable supply of bottled pure palm cooking oil.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the decision, made at the Cabinet meeting on Nov 6, followed a surge in global crude palm oil (CPO) prices, which had significantly increased production costs for manufacturers.
“Through this mechanism, we can maintain the existing ceiling prices for 1kg, 2kg, 3kg and 5kg bottles, while providing special incentives to manufacturers producing bottled cooking oil,” he told a media conference held in conjunction with the 22nd Annual General Meeting of the Malaysian Muslim Restaurant Owners Association (PRESMA) here today.
He said based on the average global CPO price of RM4,400 per tonne in October 2026, the price of a 5kg bottle of cooking oil could have risen to RM34 without the intervention.
Under the mechanism, the ceiling prices of bottled pure palm cooking oil will remain at RM6.90 for 1kg, RM13.30 for 2kg, RM19.60 for 3kg and RM30.90 for 5kg, as stipulated under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011.
Armizan said the sustained increase in global CPO prices since June 2025 had placed mounting cost pressures on manufacturers, prompting some companies to halt production of bottled cooking oil.
He said the ministry (KPDN) had worked with the Finance Ministry and other relevant ministries to implement the mechanism as an intervention to ease cost-of-living pressures amid global market disruptions caused by the conflict in West Asia.
Meanwhile, PRESMA president Datuk Mohammed Mosin Abdul Razak said stable cooking oil prices would help restaurant operators better manage their business costs.
He also hoped the government would consider introducing targeted subsidies for restaurant operators in the future, similar to the assistance provided to manufacturers. — Bernama

Title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal Jalan Kuching crash that killed lorry driver
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A car washer was brought before the Magistrate’s Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month.
Mohamad Imran Taj Maloor, 32, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan.
No plea was recorded from the accused, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44am on November 4.
The charge is framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of up to 40 years and, where the death penalty is not imposed, not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Vivi Asnita Zaina’Larifin, while the accused was represented by lawyer Azleen Farahannis.
No bail was allowed, and the court set January 28 next year for mention.
Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.
“As a result of the collision, the lorry veered onto the left road shoulder while its driver, a 39-year-old Indonesian man, suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene,” he said.
According to Mohd Zamzuri, an EBA II breath test recorded a blood alcohol reading of 61 mg/100ml for the car driver, while his passenger recorded 67 mg/100ml. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: Land acquisition must uphold rule of law, respect constitutional safeguards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Challenging decisions involving compulsory land acquisition is not an act of disloyalty but an essential part of upholding the rule of law, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said that as Malaysia continued to pursue economic growth and modernise its infrastructure, compulsory land acquisition remained a necessary but sensitive public duty requiring transparency, procedural fairness and adequate compensation.
“From the perspective of democracy, challenging the exercise of power is not an act of disloyalty, rather it’s an essential part of the rule of law,” she said at the “Challenging Land Acquisition in Malaysia” book launch here today.
She said the pace of modern development must not outstrip governance standards and constitutional guarantees.
Azalina said the completion of major infrastructure projects, including railways, industrial hubs and highways, should not be the sole measure of success, as the government must also ensure that the institutions entrusted with such powers exercised them responsibly and in accordance with the law.
She said physical progress alone did not define a country’s stature, stressing that while buildings might transform a nation’s skyline, the rule of law defined its character.
Meanwhile, she commended the legal fraternity for publishing academic and practical works that enriched jurisprudence and provided guidance to future legal practitioners. — Bernama

Title: Nadma deploys 102,000 personnel ahead of 2026/2027 northeast monsoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has mobilised nearly 102,000 personnel from various departments and agencies, along with 40,000 operational assets, in preparation for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL).
Nadma Deputy Director of Operations Datuk Dr Abdul Gapar Abu Bakar said the preparations also included 8,321 temporary relief centres nationwide, with a combined capacity of up to 1.9 million flood victims.
“Among the assets prepared are around 2,450 boats and more than 3,000 four-wheel-drive vehicles and lorries, in addition to various other supporting assets.
“We have also prepared 170,000 ready-to-eat meals as initial food supplies for victims upon their arrival at relief centres, as well as 60,000 food kits containing essential items to be distributed to victims when they return to their homes,” he said.
He was speaking after appearing on Bernama Radio’s Fokus 30 programme, titled ‘Government Preparedness for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon’, here today.
Commenting on ground-level operational coordination, Abdul Gapar said district officers are responsible for mobilising initial flood response by activating the District Disaster Operations Control Centre.
Meanwhile, the Incident Command Centre is headed by a Disaster Operations Commander, who is the district police chief, with the district Fire and Rescue Station chief serving as the deputy. The Malaysian Civil Defence Force will assist in coordinating rescue and evacuation operations.
“Apart from rescue agencies, Nadma also mobilises community leaders, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and local communities through the Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) programme to support rescue operations and the management of relief centres,” he said.
At the same time, Abdul Gapar encouraged members of the public to download the Malaysia Disaster Information Management System (MyDIMS) application, launched by Nadma on April 24, to obtain disaster-related information.
He said the application sends notifications when users are within a 10-kilometre radius of a disaster-affected area. It also consolidates weather information, disaster updates and the locations of relief centres, including navigation guidance to these centres.
In addition, residents living in high-risk areas were reminded to keep emergency bags ready, containing important documents such as identity cards and passports, basic medication, food and drinking water supplies, as well as suitable clothing, in preparation for possible flooding. — Bernama

Title: Tragedy on the Melaka campaign trail: Car hits lorry, Alor Gajah PKR deputy chief dies in crash outside campaign operations room
Article:
JASIN, Nov 11 — An aide of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka election was killed today when the car he was driving collided with a lorry, three days to voting day.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, paid tribute to J. Samivel, 62, in a Facebook post today, noting that the deceased was also Alor Gajah PKR deputy division chief.
“I have received sad news from Melaka. Brother Samivel, the representative of the Harapan candidate for the Asahan state seat, was killed in a road accident this afternoon.
“As Alor Gajah Keadilan deputy division chief, Brother Samivel had long served and remained loyal to the struggle. May his service and spirit continue to guide our steps as we carry on this struggle.
“My thoughts and prayers, and Azizah’s, are with the late Samivel’s family and fellow comrades. May they be given strength and fortitude in facing this trying ordeal,” Anwar said, speaking also for his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
The crash happened along Jalan Pondok Batang here at about noon, in front of PH’s main operations room for the Asahan seat, according to the New Straits Times.
Jasin district police chief Superintendent Lee Robert said police received information about the accident at about 12.45pm.
He said initial information showed that the car Samivel was in had collided with a lorry, which RTM reported was carrying fruit.
Lee said investigations were underway to determine the cause of the crash, and that more details would be released once police had the full picture.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said the department received an emergency call at 12.22pm.
He said rescuers found Samivel trapped in the driver’s seat, and that he was pronounced dead by Health Ministry personnel before being handed over to police.
Samivel’s body was taken to the forensic unit of Jasin Hospital for a post-mortem, the NST reported.
The PH Election Department described his death as a great loss to his family, friends, party members and everyone who knew him, the NST reported.
It also thanked him for his service and contributions, particularly his hard work throughout the state election campaign.
Sinar Harian reported that Samivel was among the “backbones” of the campaign of PH’s Asahan candidate P. Denesh.
Denesh, who was on a walkabout and house visits in Kampung Jus Permai at the time, rushed to the scene, when he heard the news.
Denesh is the challenger against Asahan incumbent from Barisan Nasional, Datuk Dr Fairul Nizam Roslan.

Title: Re-ignite the Malaysian Dream, Lim Kit Siang urges Melaka voters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Veteran DAP leader Lim Kit Siang today called on voters in Melaka to “re-ignite the Malaysian Dream”, describing Transport Minister Anthony Loke's resignation as a starting point for renewed efforts to build a united and world-class Malaysia.
In an open letter to the people of Melaka, Lim said Malaysians should embrace an identity that places nationality above ethnicity, where every citizen regards themselves as Malaysian first before identifying as Malay, Chinese, Indian, Kadazan, Iban or Orang Asli.
He said such a vision would help build a nation that is democratic, prosperous, committed to the rule of law and respectful of human rights.
Lim traced the roots of the “Malaysian Dream” to before independence, citing Chinese educationist Lim Lian Geok's 1956 message to Utusan Melayu on the need to cultivate a Malaysian mindset.
Recalling his political career, Lim said he was fielded by DAP to contest the Bandar Melaka parliamentary seat in 1969, describing the election as a battle for the Malaysian Dream.
He said he had not expected the Alliance coalition, which later became Barisan Nasional, to be defeated during his lifetime, but noted that this eventually happened in 2018, although the change in government lasted only until 2020.
According to Lim, meaningful reforms require sustained political commitment over one or two full terms in office, particularly with leaders from the country's largest community taking the lead in driving change.
While acknowledging that some reforms had been implemented, he said they did not go far enough, resulting in growing public disappointment.
Nevertheless, Lim urged Malaysians not to abandon the aspirations of the Malaysian Dream.
“I call on the voters of Malacca to represent the Malaysian nation to re-ignite the Malaysian Dream project to make Malaysia a great world-class nation by voting for every DAP and Pakatan Harapan candidate,” he said in the statement.

Title: Flood situation worsens in Selangor as evacuees increase, improves in Perak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The number of flood evacuees taking shelter at temporary relief centres (PPS) in Selangor continued to rise, while Perak recorded a decrease, as of 4 pm today.
In Selangor, the number of flood evacuees at five PPS in Kuala Selangor increased to 1,032 people, from 289 families, compared with 945 people from 265 families this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department's (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed the highest number of evacuees, at 416, followed by Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (287), SK Parit Mahang (238), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (77) and SK Jaya Setia (12).
In Perak, the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district decreased to 330 people, from 94 families, compared with 380 people, from 108 families, this morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat said that Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI) housed 257 evacuees, while Dewan MPTI Langkap accommodated 73.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast rain and thunderstorms in all districts in Perak this afternoon and evening. — Bernama

Title: Funding Malaysia’s SMEs is about quality and not quantity, says economy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government wants to improve the quality of financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to strengthen local firms’ global competitiveness and enable workers to earn higher wages and hold better-quality jobs.
Although Malaysia had recorded encouraging economic growth, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today that structural challenges still needed to be addressed so that SMEs could expand and improve productivity.
He said the main challenge was no longer simply ensuring firms had access to credit, but making sure the financing met their investment and expansion needs.
“The real issue is the quality of funding being channelled. It is not just about how firms obtain credit, but how we ensure our firms remain competitive globally.
“Particularly in ensuring productivity improvements that can eventually translate into higher wages and quality employment,” he told reporters after the launch of the World Bank’s 33rd Malaysia Economic Monitor, titled ‘From Quantity to Quality: Financing Malaysia’s Productive SMEs’, here today.
Akmal said the government had taken note of the World Bank’s recommendations, including broadening the range of assets that could be accepted as collateral.
He said relying on conventional collateral such as property could limit firms’ access to loans, even when they had other assets that could serve as security.
“Among the problems in obtaining loans is the collateral requirement, which typically requires property to be pledged as security.
“Yet firms also have other assets that should be considered, such as machinery and accounts receivable, to broaden the financing options available to them,” he said.
He added that financing mechanisms also needed to be implemented more transparently so that firms received facilities suited to their needs.
The report found that about 38 per cent of firms in Malaysia had loans or credit facilities, while loan approval rates rose from about 68 per cent in 2015 to 86 per cent in 2024.
However, it also found that SMEs still financed about two-thirds of their fixed-asset investments with internal funds, while external financing relied heavily on bank debt, with limited access to equity and other forms of risk capital.
The World Bank also highlighted that financing constraints could undermine firms’ ability to invest in innovation, improve productivity and expand.
Akmal said the push to improve financing quality was in line with the government’s aspirations under the 13th Malaysia Plan, particularly in raising productivity and strengthening economic competitiveness.
He said Malaysia’s economy remained resilient, having expanded 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, with the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s advance estimate showing 5.3 per cent growth in the third quarter.
